title: sse: fix partial JSON framing and token/event ordering in streaming responses
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: Customers (internal and external) observed malformed partial-JSON payloads when using SSE streaming for structured outputs and tool/function-calling flows. Root causes identified: (1) the streaming parser emitted delimiter tokens out-of-order when token events and delimiter events coincided, (2) the framing logic allowed a trailing delimiter to be held and combined with the next token batch producing invalid partial JSON, and (3) the OpenAI-compat adapter did not correctly translate internal token/event ordering into the expected SSE event stream ordering in some edgecases (esp. when KV cache hits reduced batch sizes).

Motivation: These bugs cause downstream JSON parsers in SDKs and customers' code to throw parse errors mid-stream (partial JSON fragments that do not follow the assumed delimiter ordering). This PR implements a small-surface backwards-compatible fix that reorders internal events deterministically, strengthens delimiter framing rules, and adds end-to-end tests against the Python and TS streaming clients.

What this PR changes (summary): - StreamParser: canonicalize event ordering such that delimiter events are always emitted before token events for the same batch boundary. This prevents partial JSON fragments where a closing delimiter arrives after token content that belongs to the next logical element. - FramingBuffer: ensure trailing delimiters are flushed atomically; prevent merging of a trailing delimiter with a subsequent token batch when the previous buffer has not been consumed. - OpenAI compatibility adapter: map internal token+event sequence to OpenAI-style SSE messages with explicit "delta" semantics; add a small buffer to coalesce token fragments into consistent partial_json fields. - SDK changes (python): defensive parsing update to accept either ordering temporarily while servers roll out. The SDK change is behind a feature-flag and does not alter public API behavior. - Docs: add streaming stability notes and recommended client-side backoff/retry for partial-parse errors.

Testing and verification: added unit tests for parser ordering, integration tests that spin up a local streaming endpoint and assert JSON validity at every SSE event boundary, and fuzz tests that emulate KV cache shaped batches. CI initially failed lint on a TS helper; fixed in followup commit. End-to-end tests (python client + local server) were run against a canary cluster; metrics show a 98% reduction in reported parse errors for affected routes.

Rollout and compatibility: This is a safe, non-breaking change. Servers and SDKs are released coordinately: server-side runtime change merged and deployed in canary the same day; python SDK release contains the feature-flaged parsing tolerance to avoid client-side breakage during rollout. We will monitor sse_partial_json_parse_failure (new metric) and a small canary cohort for 48 hours before promoting to 100%.

feat(openai-compat): coalesce token fragments into partial_json delta mapping
test(sse): add unit + integration tests for partial-json ordering
chore(docs): streaming stability notes and examples
